L1.title: Photosynthesis
L1.summary: Plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.
key_points: Light energy is captured by chlorophyll and used to make food.
The inputs are carbon dioxide and water.
The outputs include glucose and oxygen.
The process occurs mainly in leaves, in chloroplasts.
common_misconceptions: Plants take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide as the description of photosynthesis.
Plants obtain their food directly from soil.
Oxygen or glucose is described as an input rather than a product.

L2.title: Newton's First Law (Inertia)
L2.summary: An object remains at rest or continues at constant speed in a straight line unless acted on by an unbalanced external force. Inertia is resistance to change in motion; greater mass means greater inertia.
key_points: An object at rest stays at rest; a moving object continues at constant speed in a straight line.
This state continues unless an unbalanced external force acts.
The tendency to resist change in motion is called inertia.
common_misconceptions: A constant force is needed to maintain constant motion.
Moving objects naturally stop without an external force.
Inertia is itself a force that pushes objects.

L3.title: Supply and Demand
L3.summary: With supply fixed, higher demand generally raises price. With demand fixed, higher supply generally lowers price. Equilibrium is where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded; price signals help balance buyers and sellers.
key_points: Higher demand with supply unchanged generally raises price.
Higher supply with demand unchanged generally lowers price.
Equilibrium is where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded.
Price signals help balance buyers and sellers.
common_misconceptions: Higher supply always raises price, with demand held constant.
Higher demand lowers price, with supply held constant.
Demand means how much a company can produce.
